title: Building the Classes
objective: Build a Worker class and an Order class that interact with each other and report their own state.

sourceAlignment.title: JavaScript Crash Course
sourceAlignment.author: Nick Morgan
sourceAlignment.note: Original Code Forge capstone combining classes, arrays, and loops into a console-based simulation. All prose and code are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: With FoundrySettings ready, the next step is the objects that actually do the work: a Worker and an Order. A Worker has energy and a count of items completed; an Order has an id and an effort cost — how much energy it takes to finish.

A completeOrder(order) method should subtract order.effort from the worker's energy, but never let energy drop below zero — a worker at -3 energy doesn't mean anything, so clamp it to 0 with Math.max(0, ...). A separate isExhausted() method just checks whether energy has reached zero, keeping the 'can this worker keep going?' question in one place instead of repeating the comparison everywhere.

Notice that Worker and Order don't need to inherit from each other — they just happen to interact. That's fine. Inheritance is for when one class truly is a specialized version of another, not just because two classes are used together.
explanation.rule: Give every stateful object a method to change its state (completeOrder) and a method to ask about its state (isExhausted) — don't scatter that logic elsewhere.

examples.title: A Worker Completing an Order
examples.note: Math.max(0, ...) stops energy from going negative, and isExhausted() reads cleanly wherever it's used.

checks.question: A Worker has 3 energy left and completes an Order with effort 5. What should worker.energy be afterward?

feedback.correct: Correct — Math.max(0, 3 - 5) clamps the result to 0 instead of going negative.
feedback.incorrect: Without clamping, 3 - 5 would be -2, which doesn't make sense for energy — Math.max(0, ...) prevents that.

assignment.title: Worker and Order Classes
assignment.brief: Define a Worker class and an Order class. Worker should track energy and items completed; completing an order should reduce energy (never below 0) and increase the completed count.
requirements: Define class Order with a constructor(id, effort) storing both as properties.
Define class Worker with a constructor(name, energy) storing name, energy, and itemsCompleted starting at 0.
Worker needs a completeOrder(order) method that reduces energy by order.effort (clamped to a minimum of 0) and increments itemsCompleted.
Worker needs an isExhausted() method that returns true when energy is 0 or less.
assignment.outputCheckLabel: Worker("Rin", 10) completing Order(1, 4) leaves energy 6, itemsCompleted 1, isExhausted() false

hints: Order's constructor just needs to store its two arguments — nothing more.
Worker's constructor sets itemsCompleted to 0 directly, not from an argument.
completeOrder should read: this.energy = Math.max(0, this.energy - order.effort);
isExhausted() is a one-line comparison: return this.energy <= 0;
